# Design guidelines from research hwde has checked

Each line is a claim from a paper that hwde's own test, script or simulation reproduced (or reproduced in part, within the scope given). A claim hwde hasn't checked is never a guideline here; `docs/research/claims.md` lists every claim and its verdict.

- Place a bulk/MLCC anti-resonance at 1/(2 pi sqrt((L_bulk + L_mlcc) C_mlcc)) and size its peak as X^2/(ESR_bulk + ESR_mlcc), X the bulk branch's reactance there; sqrt(L/C) underestimates the peak by the circuit's Q. (in part)  
  From [Impedance analysis and optimization research of power distribution network](https://doi.org/10.1007/s42452-025-07224-6) (2025), Section 2.4, eq. 5 and the text after it; checked by `tests/test_research_claims.py::test_pdn_antiresonance_frequency_holds_magnitude_does_not` (`impedance-analysis-optimization-research-power-2025/2`).
- Damp an anti-resonance with ESR up to about sqrt((L_bulk + L_mlcc)/C_mlcc) in total, not more: past it the ESR itself sets |Z|. (in part)  
  From [Impedance analysis and optimization research of power distribution network](https://doi.org/10.1007/s42452-025-07224-6) (2025), Section 2.4 (3), Fig. 9; checked by `tests/test_research_claims.py::test_pdn_lower_q_lowers_antiresonance` (`impedance-analysis-optimization-research-power-2025/3`).
- Derate a class-II MLCC from its own bias curve (or lib/mlcc.py's density model), not a fixed share of its rated voltage: at 80 % of rating the loss runs from about 30 % on sparse parts to 80 % on dense ones. (in part)  
  From [Practical Considerations for Designing Reliable DC/DC Converters, Applied to a BIPV Case](https://doi.org/10.3390/en13040834) (2020), Section 2.2 p. 6, repeating its ref. [52] (Xu, Gu, Hernandez, Rivas-Davila); checked by `tests/test_research_claims.py::test_mlcc_80pct_bias_loss_holds_for_dense_parts_only` (`practical-considerations-designing-reliable-dc-2020/1`).
